result.summary: This unit is the upstream zlib 1.3.1 compression library: deflate/inflate, CRC-32 and Adler-32 checksums, and the gzip file API, plus generated tables and the documentation PDF. I read every source file for build-time generators, constructors, network or exec activity, encoded payloads and deviations from upstream and found none. The only file output is the documented gz* file writing to paths the caller chooses, plus table generators that run only under non-default build macros.

findings.title: Stock zlib 1.3.1 sources
findings.detail: I compared all source files in this part against the known upstream zlib 1.3.1 release: adler32, compress, crc32, deflate, the gz* files, infback, inffast, inflate, inftrees, trees, uncompr, zutil and the headers. They show no deviation from upstream: no networking, no process execution, no environment probing and no load-time constructors. The generated tables in crc32.h, trees.h and inffixed.h have the expected standard values.

findings.title: Binary PDF documentation file
findings.detail: zlib.3.pdf is the upstream manual page in PDF form, shipped in the zlib distribution. It is documentation; nothing in the reviewed sources compiles, reads or unpacks it.

findings.title: inflateUndermine is compile-time disabled by default
findings.detail: inflateUndermine() and the related permissive distance handling are standard upstream API. They do nothing unless the library is compiled with INFLATE_ALLOW_INVALID_DISTANCE_TOOFAR_ARRR; otherwise the function returns Z_DATA_ERROR and keeps sane=1.

data_flows.what: Compressed (or, in transparent mode, raw) data the caller passes to gzwrite, gzputs or gzprintf; this is the library's documented gzip file API.
data_flows.to: a file path or file descriptor chosen by the calling application (gzopen/gzdopen)

data_flows.what: Generated CRC tables. This happens only when the developer builds the table generator with MAKECRCH defined; it is not part of a normal library build.
Generated static Huffman tables. This happens only when the developer builds with GEN_TREES_H defined; it is not part of a normal library build.
